Every public and protected member reviewed. Returns the cosine, not the angle - no acos appears in the source. The source's own empty/all-zero guard (sum1 * sum2 == 0 returns 0.0) is kept verbatim, and the score is not clamped, so a spectrum against its negation scores -1.0. Deliberately not ported: the empty updateMembers_ and the dead precursor_mass_tolerance_. Native: incompatible binning is a checked Error::InvalidValue where the source only asserts through OPENMS_PRECONDITION, a release-build no-op unlike both siblings; f32 dot-product overflow is a checked error; MAX_COMPARED_BINS bounds the comparison.

The .cpp's includes of its three derived classes are factory registration, not a base-on-derivative dependency, and produce no Rust module edge.

Every public and protected member reviewed. The agreement rule is ported literally: per bin (a + b) * 0.5 - |a - b|, truncated at zero, summed, over the mean of the two totals, capped at 1.0. The walk spans the union of the stored bins because sparse addition does, the arithmetic stays f32 (Eigen promotes the scalar 0.5 down to float), and cwiseMax(0) semantics are written out rather than using f32::max. Deliberately not ported: the empty updateMembers_ and the dead precursor_mass_tolerance_. Native: a zero mean total yields 0.0 where the source returns NaN or 1.0; incompatible binning is Error::InvalidValue; f32 overflow is checked; MAX_COMPARED_BINS bounds the comparison. Negative bins are accepted as upstream, which makes an all-negative spectrum score 0 against itself - documented, because the class comment's 'perfect agreement results in 1.0' holds only for nonnegative bins.

Every declared member has its caller-side counterpart: `encode`/`decode` are the f32/f64 peak-array paths of `mzml.rs` (little endian) and `mzxml.rs` (`byteOrder="network"`, big endian), so the `ByteOrder` enum, `endianize32/64` and the `invertEndianess` specialisations are `f64::from_le_bytes`/`from_be_bytes` and their f32/i32/i64 siblings, chosen at the call site with no runtime swap; `mzdata.rs` carries the source's own `endian` attribute classification, where every spelling other than "big" reads as little (`Endian::parse`). `encodeIntegers`/`decodeIntegers` are the signed i32/i64 auxiliary arrays of `mzml.rs`; `encodeStrings`/`decodeStrings`/`decodeSingleString` are the `MS:1001479` NUL-terminated ASCII string arrays, which keep an empty element aligned with its peak where the source decoder drops an empty token. `zlib_compression` is `flate2` on the same paths, in bounded 8 KiB chunks with overrun detection and full-input consumption required. The private SIMD encoder/decoder pair has no port: `stringSimdDecoder_` is the measured 2.03x gap in docs/THIRD_PARTY_CRATE_DECISIONS.md, where `base64-simd` is recorded as measured but not adopted, since the crate is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and the benchmark build is `--locked --offline`. NOT CLAIMED: a free `Base64` facade a caller could reach for an arbitrary buffer, and byte-identical compressed output across zlib implementations. Lead decision 2026-09-21: native_equivalent means the Rust language and its standard library discharge the header, with no port owed and no third-party crate required. This header is discharged by a crate, which is a port whose implementation is a dependency, so it is recorded on member coverage instead. ReadOptions::source() names the source-compatible set, and source_invalid_timestamps defaults to true because the executed source is unconditionally lenient there: run/@startTimeStamp="-infinity", which ProteoWizard writes and which stopped every TOPP tool on the PXD001819 input at exit 6, is now read as C++ reads it (tier 1: the C++ Release FileInfo, FileConverter and MzMLSplitter on five sentinel timestamps plus a control, ../oracle/mzml-reader-scale). Adversarial documents (a declared billion points, a 4,000-fold zlib bomb, a 20,000-parameter group expanded per spectrum, 200 levels of nesting) stay refused, and InputScaling::fixed() reproduces the former ceilings exactly. ReadOptions::source_time_array_precision (fix/picked-chromatogram, merged as b1700de, default full precision, set by source()) reproduces the one other source behaviour that discards information on read: MzMLHandlerHelper::decodeBase64Arrays applies the minute multiplier of an MS:1000595 time array in place, so a 32-bit array keeps only f32 precision after the conversion while the 64-bit and Numpress paths do not (MzMLHandlerHelper.cpp:217-222, CPP-306). Tier 1 against ../oracle/picked-chromatogram: seven cases of the benchmark TIC arrays over 32/64-bit against minute/second plus the empty, single-point and unsorted shapes, read and picked by the C++ Release build, compared as IEEE-754 bit patterns, with the min32 rows pinning the source mode and the min64 rows the library default; on the 2.3 GB benchmark input the switch is what makes the two tools' picked TIC chromatograms bit-identical. A finite 32-bit time whose product with 60 is not finite is refused rather than stored as the source's infinity. WRITER (fix/mzml-writer-scale-parity, 522ce8f, docs/MZML_WRITER_CPP_PARITY.md): the writer's budgets became per-record, so 50,000 realistic records now store through every default entry point where the fixed ceiling refused at about 650; mzml::write and therefore FileHandler::store_experiment and every mzML-writing TOPP tool write indexedmzML with record offsets and a real SHA-1 fileChecksum in one pass, as MzMLFile::store does with its default PeakFileOptions - the source writes the constant 0 there (CPP-049) and its indexListOffset addresses the newline before the tag (CPP-305), so both container fields differ by construction and D6 reports them as container facts. The port also stopped inventing a zero precursor intensity. Six HPC tests in these two targets are #[ignore]d because they read the staged benchmark inputs under /ceph on the IBMI nodes. Wave 4 (perf/mzml-reader, perf/validation): the reader was rewritten without changing a decoded value - buffer reuse across records, decode_slice in place of decode_vec's zero fill, and a base64 accumulation that no longer pushes one char at a time - for -47.2% of the instructions the load path executed, measured by callgrind on a fixed slice with a layout control; on the wave-4 benchmark the port's load of a 1.2 GB mzML is now faster than the C++ reader's (FileInfo 12.807 s against 15.951 s at one thread, output byte-equal). The reader's per-record spectrum.validate() was then REMOVED, not weakened: every decoded float already reaches Record::finish through a decode-time refusal of nonfinite values (mzml.rs:822/:965/:310), so both the m/z and the intensity half of that loop were dead over all 197,765,338 points of the benchmark input. The argument is written into the rustdoc at the call site and pinned by a 36-probe test in tests/mzml.rs whose premise is mutation-checked; the removal is worth -44,121,898 instructions (15.0 Ir per peak) and the branch as a whole -60,947,537 (-1.605%) against its merge base. The zip crate reads the central directory; the single non-directory entry is decoded by the port (stored, deflate via flate2, bzip2) with libzip's end-of-entry CRC-32 and size checks. zip_fread semantics: a read fills unless the entry ends, the stream closes only on a read of 0 (the header's 'short read closes' is not what the implementation does), n == 0 is a no-op even when closed, a CRC failure is reported after the bytes. src/openms/include/OpenMS/FORMAT/ZlibCom.scope: `flate2 =1.1` discharges the static utility class outright, so no `ZlibCompression` type exists. `compressString`/`compressData` are the `ZlibEncoder` writes of the mzML and Numpress encoders; `uncompressData`/`uncompressString` are their `Decompress`/`FlushDecompress` reads. The source's two decompression paths (iterative when `output_size == 0`, single preallocated buffer when it is known) collapse into one bounded 8 KiB chunked loop that requires a complete stream with a matching checksum and full input consumption, so trailing or concatenated compressed data is rejected rather than silently accepted; the source's gzip-framing refusal is kept, and `path_io::open` separately sniffs gzip/bzip2 magic for whole-file input. NATIVE, deliberate: the source's OutOfMemory / InvalidValue / ConversionError / InternalToolError quartet becomes checked `Error` values against a declared ceiling rather than worst-case `compressBound` allocation, and the informational log line the source writes when the actual size is below `output_size` has no counterpart. NOT CLAIMED: byte-identical compressed output — the compressed bytes may differ from the source's zlib while decompressing identically. Lead decision 2026-09-21: native_equivalent means the Rust language and its standard library discharge the header, with no port owed and no third-party crate required. This header is discharged by a crate, which is a port whose implementation is a dependency, so it is recorded on member coverage instead. Complete: all four declared members have a caller-side counterpart.

A5b re-audit 2026-09-28 (wave 4), header read member by member at core bc9cc12 against the current Rust. The three members the earlier scope listed as missing are now ported, and no other public member is missing (constructors, copy/move and assignment, the fifteen register* and get*s members, addScore, the current-step trio, getBestMatchPerObservation, getMatchesForObservation, the two remove*If templates, findScoreType, calculateCoverages, cleanup, empty, merge, swap, clear, the three setMetaValue overloads, removeMetaValue and the MetaInfoInterface base were each checked against the Rust). (1) pickScoreType is IdentificationData::pick_score_type(container, all_elements, any_score) over any iterator of &ScoredProcessingResult (src/identification/graph/apply.rs), resolving each most recent score through the graph's software priorities; Ok(None) is getScoreTypes().end(). Native difference: with counting enabled the source returns max_element over std::map<ScoreTypeRef, Size>, whose std::pair operator< compares the key first, so it returns the counted type with the highest set-node ADDRESS and never consults the counts (IdentificationData.h:599-602); the port implements the documented contract (highest count, tie to the later-registered type). The only in-tree caller, MapAlignmentAlgorithmIdentification.cpp:120, uses the defaults, where no counting happens. (2) applyToObservations is apply_to_observations(FnMut(&mut Observation)), one transaction: changed keys are re-sorted with stable ObservationIds; an invalid record, a foreign input file, a limit violation or a key collision leaves the graph unchanged. Native difference: the source's Boost.MultiIndex modify erases an element whose new key collides, leaving any observation match that referenced it dangling. (3) RefTranslator::allow_missing is the public ReferenceTranslator::allow_missing flag (default false): molecule() and observation_match() - the two translate overloads - return the old ID unchanged when it is set (IdentificationData.cpp:1387, :1396); every other table is a plain std::map in the source and stays an error. BaseFeature/FeatureMap/ConsensusMap update_id_references inherit the flag through those two lookups, as updateIDReferences does in the source. processing::smoothing::SavitzkyGolayFilter ports the iterator template filter(first, last, d_first) as filter(&[f64], &[f64]) -> Vec<f64>, the MSSpectrum and MSChromatogram overloads (filter_spectrum, filter_chromatogram) and filterExperiment (SpectrumFilter::filter_experiment over spectra and chromatograms), with the source defaults frame_size 11 and order 4. The source's exact window scheme is reproduced: the whole signal is returned unchanged when it is shorter than the frame; the first half-window uses the first complete window evaluated at successive positions and the last half-window the reflected edge coefficients of the last complete window; interior points use the centred row; every output is clamped at zero by std::max(0.0, help); the fit runs over sample indices, not physical coordinates, so non-uniform positions are accepted and preserved but not resampled; an even frame length is increased by one, including zero becoming one. Coefficients come from a twice-orthogonalised QR on a scaled Vandermonde basis, which solves the same full-rank least-squares problem as the source's Eigen SVD; bit-identical coefficients are explicitly not promised. Native: frame lengths up to 1023 and degrees up to 32, rank-deficient fits refused, spectrum type left unchanged. src/openms/include/OpenMS/SYSTEM/StopWat.scope: Every public member and the private TimeDiff_ surface have a documented Rust counterpart, and all 21 class-test sections are mapped. Partial, not complete, for one reason: the source reaches the per-process user/kernel split through POSIX times() on every Unix, while this port reads /proc/self/stat on Linux and reports user_time/system_time as None on macOS, other Unix and Windows (cpu_time still answers there from the aggregate process CPU clock). Restoring the split needs a libc dependency, which is the integrator's decision. PartialOrd is deliberately not implemented because the source's operator< compares CPU time alone and would disagree with its own operator==.
